simple.meaning: דּוֹנַג (dôwnag) is a Hebrew word meaning “wax ;.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: דּוֹנַג (H1749) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 22:15, with occurrences in Psalms, Micah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוֹנַג (H1749) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in דּוֹנַג (H1749) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: דּוֹנַג (dôwnag) / H1749 is traced through Psalms 22:15, Psalms 68:3, Psalms 97:5, Micah 1:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1749. donag דּוֺנַג noun masculine wax , דּוֺנַג Micah 1:4 2 t.; דּוֺנָג֑ Psa 22:15 — always in simile, of melting; at theophany hills melt like wax 97:5 ; like wax before fire Micah 1:4 ; wicked perish as wax melteth before fire Psa 68:3 ; heart melteth like wax 22:15 (simile of fear, despair). On ׳ד in 118:12 compare Bae Che critical note .
